summary: Unexpected cross-region egress for LatAm-pinned embedding job causing sporadic latency spikes
description: Customer EduWave reports that bulk embedding jobs scheduled in their LatAm dedicated pool (sa-east-1) intermittently egress to our us-east fallback pool despite having region pinning enabled. This behavior correlates with sporadic 200–600ms tail latency spikes on their embedding pipeline and occasional tokenization errors reported by the client SDK. Customer is concerned about both performance and data residency guarantees for a subset of PII-containing training data.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a dedicated embedding job in EduWave account with region pin set to sa-east-1 and model redwood-embed-v1
2) Submit a batch of 8k short texts (50–200 tokens each) via the bulk embeddings endpoint with parallelism 16
3) Observe normal routing decisions for first ~90k requests, then occasional requests show 'route: fallback-us-east-1' in response headers
4) When fallback routing occurs, measure per-request latency and compare token-level latencies to sa-east-1 routed requests
5) Check platform routing logs and request trace id shown in SDK when anomalous response occurs

investigation_notes: Capacity snapshot: sa-east-1 dedicated pool reported 78% GPU utilization during reported window, with autoscaler provisioning lag of ~30s for queued requests.
Routing policy: EduWave account was configured with regional_pin=sa-east-1 but strict_pin flag was not enabled; default behavior allows fallback to nearest region when capacity is constrained.
KV cache evidence: Several fallback routed traces included kv-cache-miss on model shards which increased generation latency and triggered fallback decision due to predicted SLA miss.

Tokenization errors appear only on fallback path due to a mismatch in tokenizer version between sa-east-1 and us-east-1 pools for open-llama-7b; redwood-embed-v1 unaffected for tokenization but saw increased latency.
Observed correlation: spikes coincide with EduWave's large nightly batches that temporarily exceed threshold that triggers regional failover in our policy engine.
resolution: Short-term: Applied a per-account routing override to strongly prefer sa-east-1 for EduWave during their nightly window (00:00-06:00 local) and advised customer to reduce parallelism from 16 -> 8 for large batches. Medium-term: Engineering will add a 'strict_residency' toggle for dedicated pools (behaves as hard pin: reject or queue rather than fallback) and will coordinate tokenizer version sync across regions. Patch PR created (see related_github_prs). Follow-up: schedule a configuration review with EduWave to confirm policy and update billing note for potential queuing delays.
